facts.raw_span: no history of abdominal surgery, trauma, or chronic illness
localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure
small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right
abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery
no history of abdominal surgery, trauma, or chronic illness
localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure
small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right
abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right, and an abnormal superior mesenteric artery-vein relationship, are consistent with intestinal malrotation.

The patient's symptoms, including localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium, positive McBurney's sign, and rebound tenderness, are consistent with acute appendicitis, although the appendix appeared normal on imaging.
The patient's imaging findings, including mesenteric congestion with prominent vessels, are consistent with mesenteric congestion, although there were no signs of ischemia.

The patient's symptoms, including acute hypogastric pain, nausea, and occasional postprandial abdominal discomfort, are consistent with gastroenteritis, although the patient's white-cell count was elevated.
The normal appearance of the appendix and the abnormal positioning of the small-bowel loops and mesenteric vessels suggest an internal hernia.

rationales.F12: Normal appearance of the appendix rules out acute appendicitis.
